title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: Embedding Visualization & Evaluation
summary: Key Insights: Word2Vec: Best for semantic analogies; FastText: Best for rare words and syntactic; GloVe: Fast training but slightly lower quality; BERT: Best overall (but contextual, not static)

sections.title: Why Evaluate Embeddings?
sections.body:
**Goal**: Visualize embeddings and measure their quality.

### Questions to Answer:
```
1. Are similar words/sentences close together?
2. Do embeddings capture semantic relationships?
3. How do different models compare?
4. Are embeddings useful for downstream tasks?
```

### Two Types of Evaluation:

**Intrinsic**: Test embeddings directly
```
• Word similarity tasks
• Word analogy tasks
• Clustering quality
• Visualization
```

**Extrinsic**: Test on downstream tasks
```
• Text classification accuracy
• Sentiment analysis performance
• Named Entity Recognition F1
• Information retrieval metrics
```

sections.title: Visualization Methods
sections.body:
### 1. PCA (Principal Component Analysis)
```
✓ Fast and deterministic
✓ Linear dimensionality reduction
✓ Good for initial exploration
✗ May not capture complex patterns
```

### 2. t-SNE (t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding)
```
✓ Excellent for visualization
✓ Preserves local structure
✓ Reveals clusters clearly
✗ Slow for large datasets
✗ Non-deterministic
✗ Can't transform new points
```

### 3. UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection)
```
✓ Faster than t-SNE
✓ Preserves global + local structure
✓ Can transform new points
✓ More consistent
```

sections.title: Intrinsic Evaluation: Word Similarity
sections.body:
### Popular Datasets:

**WordSim-353**
```
• 353 word pairs
• Human similarity ratings
• Example: ("computer", "software") → 8.5/10
```

**SimLex-999**
```
• 999 word pairs
• Focus on genuine similarity (not relatedness)
• Example: ("car", "automobile") → high similarity
```

**RW (Rare Words)**
```
• 2,034 word pairs
• Tests handling of rare words
• Challenge for Word2Vec/GloVe
```

### Evaluation Metric: Spearman Correlation

```python
# Human ratings
human_scores = [8.5, 7.2, 6.1, ...]

# Model similarity scores
model_scores = [0.85, 0.68, 0.59, ...]

# Correlation (higher = better)
correlation = spearmanr(human_scores, model_scores)
# Good: > 0.7
# Excellent: > 0.8
```

sections.title: Intrinsic Evaluation: Word Analogies
sections.body:
### Google Analogy Dataset

**Semantic analogies**:
```
capital-common-countries:
  Athens - Greece + Norway = Oslo

capital-world:
  Baghdad - Iraq + India = Delhi

currency:
  Angola - kwanza + Brazil = real

city-in-state:
  Chicago - Illinois + Texas = Houston
```

**Syntactic analogies**:
```
comparative:
  bad - worse + good = better
  big - bigger + small = smaller

superlative:
  bad - worst + good = best
  big - biggest + small = smallest

present-participle:
  dance - dancing + work = working
  
past-tense:
  dancing - danced + working = worked
```

### Evaluation:

```python
# Test: king - man + woman = ?
result = model.most_similar(positive=['king', 'woman'], 
                            negative=['man'], topn=1)
# Correct if result[0] == 'queen'

Accuracy = Correct answers / Total questions
```

sections.title: Typical Benchmark Results
sections.body:
### Word Similarity (Spearman Correlation):

| Model | WS-353 | SimLex-999 | RW |
|-------|---------|------------|-----|
| Word2Vec-300d | 0.687 | 0.443 | 0.538 |
| GloVe-300d | 0.623 | 0.404 | 0.478 |
| FastText-300d | 0.658 | 0.442 | **0.571** |
| BERT (contextual) | **0.731** | **0.502** | 0.556 |

### Word Analogies (Accuracy %):

| Model | Semantic | Syntactic | Total |
|-------|----------|-----------|-------|
| Word2Vec-300d | **74.2** | 70.3 | **72.5** |
| GloVe-300d | 71.5 | 63.1 | 67.9 |
| FastText-300d | 72.8 | **72.1** | 72.5 |

**Key Insights**:
- Word2Vec: Best for semantic analogies
- FastText: Best for rare words and syntactic
- GloVe: Fast training but slightly lower quality
- BERT: Best overall (but contextual, not static)

sections.title: Extrinsic Evaluation: Downstream Tasks
sections.body:
### Common Benchmark Tasks:

**Text Classification**:
```
• 20 Newsgroups
• IMDB sentiment
• AG News
→ Measure: Accuracy, F1
```

**Named Entity Recognition**:
```
• CoNLL-2003
• OntoNotes
→ Measure: F1 score
```

**Semantic Textual Similarity**:
```
• STS Benchmark
• SICK
→ Measure: Spearman correlation
```

**Question Answering**:
```
• SQuAD
• Natural Questions
→ Measure: Exact Match, F1
```

sections.title: Evaluation Metrics Summary
sections.body:
### For Classification:
```python
Accuracy = Correct / Total
Precision = TP / (TP + FP)
Recall = TP / (TP + FN)
F1 = 2 * (Precision * Recall) / (Precision + Recall)
```

### For Similarity:
```python
Cosine Similarity = (A · B) / (||A|| ||B||)
Spearman Correlation = Rank correlation
Pearson Correlation = Linear correlation
```

### For Retrieval:
```python
Precision@K = Relevant in top K / K
Recall@K = Relevant in top K / Total relevant
MAP = Mean Average Precision
NDCG = Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain
```

sections.title: Visualization Best Practices
sections.body:
### PCA Guidelines:
```python
✓ Use for quick exploration
✓ Plot first 2-3 components
✓ Check explained variance
✓ Good for linear patterns
```

### t-SNE Guidelines:
```python
✓ Tune perplexity (5-50 typical)
✓ Run multiple times (non-deterministic)
✓ Don't over-interpret distances
✓ Use for publication-quality figures
⚠️ Perplexity: 5-50 (larger dataset → larger perplexity)
⚠️ Iterations: 1000+ for convergence
```

### UMAP Guidelines:
```python
✓ Balance between PCA and t-SNE
✓ Faster than t-SNE
✓ Better preserves global structure
✓ Can embed new points
⚠️ n_neighbors: 5-50 (local structure sensitivity)
⚠️ min_dist: 0.0-0.99 (cluster tightness)
```

sections.title: Practical Evaluation Pipeline
sections.body:
### Step-by-Step:

**1. Intrinsic Evaluation (Fast)**
```python
# Test on word similarity benchmark
correlation = evaluate_similarity(model, 'wordsim353')
# Good if > 0.65

# Test analogies
accuracy = evaluate_analogies(model, 'google_analogies')
# Good if > 0.60
```

**2. Visualization**
```python
# Visualize with t-SNE
plot_tsne(model, words=['king', 'queen', ...])
# Check if clusters make sense
```

**3. Extrinsic Evaluation (Slow but definitive)**
```python
# Train classifier with embeddings
accuracy = train_classifier(model, 'imdb')
# Compare with baseline
```

sections.title: Choosing the Best Embedding
sections.body:
### Decision Matrix:

| Priority | Choose |
|----------|--------|
| **Speed** | GloVe-50d |
| **OOV handling** | FastText |
| **General quality** | Word2Vec-300d |
| **Rare words** | FastText |
| **Best overall** | BERT (contextual) |
| **Small file** | GloVe-50d |
| **Morphology** | FastText |

### Quick Comparison Recipe:

```python
# 1. Load multiple embeddings
models = {
    'word2vec': load_word2vec(),
    'glove': load_glove(),
    'fasttext': load_fasttext(),
}

# 2. Test on your specific task
for name, model in models.items():
    score = evaluate_on_task(model, your_task)
    print(f"{name}: {score}")

# 3. Pick the winner!
```

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
### ❌ Don't:
```
✗ Use only intrinsic evaluation
✗ Ignore downstream task performance
✗ Over-interpret t-SNE plots
✗ Compare embeddings of different dimensions directly
✗ Forget to normalize vectors
```

### ✅ Do:
```
✓ Test on YOUR specific task
✓ Use multiple evaluation methods
✓ Consider speed/quality tradeoff
✓ Normalize embeddings before similarity
✓ Report multiple metrics
```

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.body:
### For Static Word Embeddings:
```
1. Word2Vec: Best general purpose
2. GloVe: Fastest training
3. FastText: Best for OOV and rare words
```

### For Sentence Embeddings:
```
1. SBERT: Best quality and ease of use
2. USE: Good alternative
3. Averaged Word2Vec: Fast baseline
```

### Evaluation Strategy:
```
1. Start with intrinsic (quick sanity check)
2. Visualize (understand what's captured)
3. Test on YOUR task (definitive answer)
4. Consider speed/quality tradeoff
```
